chose: refactor pipeline: 2 steps (enrich, llm-enrich) with run bodies inlined in workflow index.ts, helpers flat in lib/, backfill becomes a CLI script
over: flattening atproto-sync's flow graph into one job
because: backfill/report are job triggers not steps; user wants index.ts readable as a high-level narrative; atproto-sync's finalize genuinely needs waiting-children for its fold+reconcile+lock release

chose: pipeline gets a Fastify plugin DI spine: app.ts composition root + @fastify/autoload for plugins/ and workflows/, defineWorkflow becomes fastify.workflow(spec) modelled on orange-api notifications' plugins/sqs.ts
over: keeping the lazy module-singleton + manual-teardown pattern (six resources, three entrypoints, each teardown called by hand in 3 places)
three separate app files, one per entrypoint
because: one pg pool instead of two, requireRedis()'s runtime ordering contract becomes a boot-time plugin dependency, and adding a workflow becomes adding a folder instead of editing a registry array. Plan: docs/plans/2026-08-27-pipeline-fastify-di.md

chose: plugins/env.ts parses process.env with zod, not @fastify/env
because: repo already depends on zod 4 and nothing in it uses ajv; @fastify/env drags in env-schema+ajv for an identical fastify.env decorator and identical fail-at-boot behavior

chose: @fastify/autoload may not discover .ts files under Node native type-stripping — this service runs node src/server.ts with no build step
couldBe: the instrument is wrong — the thing that PRODUCED this number, not the thing it describes
autoload globs a fixed extension list that excludes .ts, needing an explicit matchFilter/extensions option; or it works unmodified because it resolves via dynamic import()
discriminatedBy: register autoload against a src/plugins/ dir with one trivial .ts plugin and check whether its decorator exists after app.ready()

because: food already owns the domain vocabulary and the classifiers are pure functions over it. Measured three duplicated spellings across the boundary: AllergenSlug (identical 10-string union in food/src/traits.ts:19 and pipeline types.ts:69), TriState (traits.ts:16 and types.ts:21), and IngredientTraits vs FoodTraits — the last declared structurally on purpose so a classifier would not depend on where traits come from, a reason that evaporates once the classifier lives in the same package as the traits

chose: autoload works directly on .ts files under node's native TS stripping — no build step, no compiled-dir indirection needed
because: throwaway spike: @fastify/autoload registered against a dir with one fp-wrapped .ts plugin, run via 'node src/_spike/run.ts' (no build step, Node 26 native TS type-stripping), app.ready() resolved and the decorator was present

chose: implemented Phase 1 and Phase 2 as one pass, verified once at the end
over: verifying green after Phase 1 alone, with workflow modules still calling defineWorkflow()/getPool() singletons
because: the plan's own phase split is interdependent: D4 (fastify.db inside workflow steps) requires fastify in scope inside index.ts/steps.ts, which only exists once those modules become plugins (D6, filed under Phase 2). Honoring the split would mean inventing a throwaway singleton-getter shim in Phase 1 just to delete it in Phase 2 — more churn than value. Converted db/redis/posthog/ai plugins and the workflow plugins together, single typecheck+test pass at the end

chose: capture.ts split: only AI_GENERATION_EVENT + Usage/Pricing/Error types + envFloat moved to lib/ai/capture.ts
over: moving buildGenerationEvent/sendGenerationEvent wholesale to lib/ai/capture.ts as the plan's §5 wording suggests
because: GenerationEventInput's fields and buildGenerationEvent's output properties (recipe_id, prompt_name, labels_written, disagreements, line_count, unresolved_line_count) and PIPELINE_DISTINCT_ID are already saturated with recipe-enrichment-specific names — none are generic AI-capture concepts. Moving them into a folder that claims genericity would misrepresent them; kept them in the workflow's own capture.ts, only swapping the captureEvent import for a posthog-port parameter

chose: plugins/ai.ts owns the memoized Prompts client; lib/ai/prompt-fetch.ts is a pure function taking client+promptName+fallbackText
over: keeping prompt-fetch.ts's module-level memoized client + resetPromptCache when moving it to src/lib/ai/
because: D0: nothing in src/lib/ may hold process-global mutable state. The memoized Prompts client and the warn-once flag are lifecycle state, so they belong in the plugin closure (fastify.ai.fetchPrompt), not in lib/. Updated prompt-fetch.test.ts to call the pure fn directly with an explicit client instead of resetPromptCache()

because: classify.ts aggregates classifiers/index.ts which aggregates allergen.ts/diet.ts which need the vocabulary types; importing from classify.ts itself would create a module cycle even though import-type erases at runtime — mirrors the original pipeline's types.ts-as-sibling-file design

over: re-exporting them from classify.ts for a single import surface
because: src/index.ts's barrel does export * from both traits.ts and classify.ts; re-exporting the same name from both would be an ambiguous star-export collision. Consumers get them from traits.ts instead
